newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares close up on improved sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares close up on improved sentiment.

text.p: Shanghai's foreign currency B shares closed up 1.5 percent on Thursday after an improvement in market sentiment saw retail investors picking up cheap shares, brokers said.
Growing speculation that the government believes recent falls were overdone and would seek to prevent sharp fluctuations in the future helped boost sentiment, they said.
The B share index closed up 1.115 points or 1.51 percent to 74.841 points on volume of 14.529 million shares worth $7.696 million.
"Market sentiment has improved somewhat with two days of gains," said a broker at a foreign securities firm.
"Institutions did not sell heavily when the index fell sharply recently so after retail selling slowed, the index began to bounce off the lows," he said.

B shares rebounded on Wednesday after steady falls since the July 1 handover of the former British colony of Hong Kong to Chinese rule. The handover, the subject of a nationwide media frenzy, had been a major market support.

Market rumours that the official Xinhua news agency had issued a directive ordering journalists and analysts not to spook the markets with negative news as share speculation was already under control had also helped sentiment, they said.
The rumours could not be confirmed.
"The key reason for today's rise is that many shares were oversold, so a rebound was a rational expectation," said the foreign securities firm broker.
Of 45 B shares, 40 traded with 25 up, 12 down and three flat.
Textile maker Shanghai Worldbest Co was the top B share gainer on institutional buying, rising $0.046 or 9.13 percent to $0.550.
Newcomer Jinan Qingqi Motorcycle was the most actively traded on bargain hunting. It rose $0.028 or 6.36 percent to $0.468 on volume of around 1.5 million shares.
Meanwhile, the domestic currency A share index reversed earlier gains to close lower on profit taking caused by talk a listed firm would be punished for reporting false results, brokers said.
The A index fell 1.212 points or 0.10 percent to 1,169.989 points on volume of 304.2 million shares worth 3.519 billion yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index lost 21.944 points or 0.59 percent to 3,692.078 points.
The A and B share markets could move up slowly as investors started to focus on companies expected to post good 1997 interim results later this month and in August, brokers said.
"Companies' interim reports are now the focus of the market and shares expected to post good results will see gains in the near future," a trader with a major Shanghai brokerage said.
